title: The Rise of E-Sports
content: A few decades ago, playing video games was simply a hobby for teenagers. Today, competitive gaming, known as e-sports, has become a global phenomenon. Professional gamers practice for up to 10 hours a day and can earn millions of dollars in prize money and sponsorships. Major e-sports tournaments fill enormous stadiums with enthusiastic fans, and millions more watch the matches live on streaming platforms like Twitch. Some universities even offer scholarships for talented players. Critics argue that e-sports shouldn't be considered "real" sports because they don't involve physical exertion. However, supporters point out that competitive gaming requires intense concentration, fast reflexes, and complex teamwork.
